recipes.name: Sausage Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (28 ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes with juice

steps.text: Cook and stir sausage in a soup pot over medium heat until crumbly and no longer pink.
Add onions, celery, and carrots. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft, about 5 minutes.
Add broth, tomatoes, cabbage, and basil; bring to a boil. Stir in pasta; cover and simmer until pasta is tender, about 10 minutes. Season with garlic salt.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage Soup
raw_recipe.description: This Italian sausage soup recipe is made with chicken broth, bow-tie pasta, tomatoes, carrots, and shredded cabbage seasoned with basil and garlic.

review.reviewBody: AWESOME SOUP!! While browning the italian sausage, I added the celery/carrots/onions, which slightly sped up the cooking process and used (the wonderfully convenient=my personal favorite) pre-shredded/pre-packaged coleslaw mix. I had to add a little more liquid (I just added additional water) as it started to get a little too thick towards the end but the taste was spectacular!! A few family members garnished with some shredded cheddar cheese over each bowl. Would make again and highly recommend!! Thanks Behr for sharing this recipe! Perfectly satisfying!!

This was DELICIOUS! I used 1 pound of ground Italian sausage plus 1 pound of kielbasa sausage cut into bite sized pieces. I used (2) 14 oz cans of fire roasted tomatoes (love the flavor!), I only used 4 cups of chicken broth - I like a really thick soup. I used 1 teaspoon of garlic salt, 2 heaping teaspoons of minced fresh garlic, about 3 tablespoons of Italian seasoning. The pasta would taste good, but has no nutritional value, so I used brown rice instead - I cooked 1 cup of brown rice in 2 1/2 cups of water SEPARATELY then added it to the soup when the rice was done. I did not use celery, but instead I cut a head of cabbage in half, then chopped up half a head and added that to the soup (much more cabbage than 1 1/2 cups) I added a small can of chopped hatch green chilis - just enough to add a tiny bit of heat to the soup. Sooo good! Thank you!

Delicious! I added chopped green/red/yellow pepper and fresh sliced mushrooms. Used hot Italian sausage instead of mild. And replaced the whole tomatoes with 2(14 ounce) cans diced tomatoes with garlic and basil. I cooked the macaroni separately and added it to the soup in the individual servings.

this soup was really good. i made it last night and put it in the crock pot. I browned the Italian sausage first. the only changes I made I added one bell pepper instead of one of the onions. instead of whole tomatoes I added 2 cans of dieced tomatoes one of the can of tomatoes had green chillies.
I left out the basil and added a bay leaf after soup was done. I took out the Bay leaf. I cooked my noodles separate and the noodles to my bowl. 
I will make this again

I'll make this again! Didn't have cabbage, so did as someone else suggested and used spinach--a bag of frozen spinach added near the end. Used ditalinin pasta cooked separately i stead of bow tie. Used one can diced, and one can stewed tomatoes that I cut up with my kitchen scissors, because that's what I had on hand. I should have sauteed the veggies longer, but the soup was delicious!!

We loved this. I make a lot of soups but this was a bit different than what I've made before. I did add fresh garlic and used diced tomatoes and added about 14 oz additional tomatoes and 1 c. Extra chicken broth. Then I added the mini farfale and it was perfect. It actually had more broth to it than it looks in the pic. Great recipe. Adding it to our favorite soups!

Good recipe. I followed the recipe except that I used fresh garlic instead of garlic salt, and cooked the pasta separately. I think that soup improves with time, so I prepared it with everything except the pasta earlier in the day and let it mellow. Near serving time, I added the pasta and cooked until hot. It was easy and very flavorful. I will make this again.

This was delicious! I added a lot more fluid than the recipe called for but otherwise the soup would’ve been too thick. I used two 32 ounce containers of chicken broth (8 cups), and two more cups of water. At the very end my wife added a tablespoon of dried tomato bullion and some Italian seasoning. Can’t stop eating this!

This is one of the best soups I've ever eaten store bought, restaurant, or homemade. I agree with others to add more seasonings. I don't like the taste of basil but I loooove garlic! So I did 1 tsp basil, 1 tsp parsley, 1 tsp. garlic salt, 1 tsp. garlic powder, and a dash of rosemary. I found the combo really nice! Flavorful without being too much. I don't think the recipe said this, but I sliced the sausage into little "coin shaped" pieces. I cooked all veggies listed plus added 2 green zucchini and in the last 10 mins of cook time added 1 bag of spinach as well. I think if you are going to cook carrots and zucchini all the way through, it is necessary to cook the soup more like 20 mins. Boil for 10, simmer for 10. This works out well because it gives you a chance to make some garlic bread to go with! Also, if you like lots of broth, you may way to add 3 more cups of chicken broth but again that depends on your preferences. AMAZING soup! I will definitely be making this on a regular basis!

Very tasty! Mine ended up more like a stew than a soup as I added only about 4 cups liquid (I planned it that way). I used beef broth as suggested by others. 

I added 2 lbs sausage, only 1 small can diced tomatoes and used a combo of slow cook rice and orzo (equaling 2 cups). I also added thinly sliced baby zucchini, garlic powder, parsley, black pepper and salt as I did not have garlic salt. I absolutely loved the cabbage on this. 

I know my variations would not have mattered had the base recipe not been great. Thanks for sharing this with us. Can't wait for leftovers tonight!

Was only fairly tasty - so I zipped it up a bit with some herbs and seasonings. I would advise against cooking the pasta in the soup as the residual starch makes it too thick. Continue to simmer the soup while cooking pasta in a separate pot. Obviously drain pasta before adding to soup. Also, since we have our own herbs, I used a good bit of fresh basil leaves, parsley and even a bit of rosemary- and it was fabulous. Decided to use the mini farfalle (bow ties) considering that the tomatoes were huge already. Next time I will use diced tomatoes instead as well. Everything is easier to manage with bite sizes when eating soup. Serve with crusty Italian bread and real butter. Great comfort food on a cold day. :)
Great recipe- I added some cannellini beans and a little crushed red pepper too and it was perfect!

I used two cups of red lentils and I needed all that broth. I noticed other people cut the amount of broth, but with the lentils you need the broth. Otherwise I made this "as is" . Since groceries are so expensive right now, I cut up the cabbage and other non-meat items and put it all in freezer bags. so all the raw ingredients are prepped. Just add sausage and broth when ready to cook.
Delicious! Good hearty soup wonderful with a crusty bread on a cold day. Only substitute I made was I only had a can of crushed tomatoes instead of whole tomatoes. Still quite lovely!
My family loved this. Definitely will make again.

I made this recipe as written using gluten free bow tie pasta and hot Italian sausage. To prepare, I smooshed the tomatoes instead of leaving whole. This recipe is a good base or start but even with hot sausage it was on the blander side. The only flavor really came from the sausage. In addition, no one in my family liked the big chunks of tomatoes, diced tomatoes would work better in this recipe. My family rated this recipe a 3, it was okay, but no-one really liked it.

I could not find Italian hotdogs because I do not really know anything about Italy, so I used American hotdogs instead. I replaced the pasta with more hotdogs and cocktail sausages for extra protein. Really simple and hearty!
I had some 4 pepper polish sausage that I wanted to use up so I chopped up the entire link. It added a little spice to it.
Substituted bell pepper for cabbage.
I took out the cabbage and carrots. Added black beans, minced garlic, a jalapeno, and sweet bell peppers. Seasoned with italian herbs and a bbq rub. Very hearty and tasty.
